House: 62/100 (learned heat loss vs configured +15; thermal-mass correction −3)
House: the envelope's heat loss in W/K, corrected for thermal mass, against what is typical for the configured house type and building era. 50 is typical for that type and era; above is tighter, below leakier. Never 0 — that is only for no data.

Heat pump: — Not enough COP data yet to watch the heat pump. (samples per outdoor band, 20 needed: -3 to 0 °C 12, 0 to 3 °C hot water 5, 3 to 6 °C 4, -6 to -3 °C 2; 7 refused while learning was frozen)
Heat pump: the measured COP — heat delivered per kWh of electricity — in each 3 °C outdoor band, against the pump's own history in that band. 100 is matching its history; each point below is a lasting COP shortfall (see the COP health diagnostics). A band is watched once it holds 20 samples; no grade yet means no band does — not a zero.

Driving: 60/100 (energy bought below the day's mean price +70; energy bought above the day's mean price −10)
Driving: whether the plan buys at the cheap hours. Each day's energy is priced against that day's flat mean spot price — buying 20% below flat scores 100, at or above flat scores 0 — and the grade averages recent days. No grade means no priced day scored yet — not a zero.
